subject: community-medicine
title: Coefficient of Variation, Interquartile Range, and Percentiles

steps.title: Coefficient of variation defined
steps.tx: The **coefficient of variation** divides the standard deviation by the mean and multiplies by one hundred, expressing spread as a percentage of the average. Being unit free, it compares variability across unlike quantities: height against weight, haemoglobin against cholesterol, or two laboratory assays in different units. Below five percent suggests tight consistency in most biological and assay contexts, though context always judges.
steps.say: Coefficient of variation is standard deviation as a percent of the mean. No units, so unlike quantities become comparable.

steps.title: Comparing two series with CV
steps.tx: The classic use is **comparing variability with coefficient of variation**: infants' weights (mean five kilograms, SD one) vary relatively more than adults' (mean sixty, SD six), because twenty percent beats ten percent despite the smaller absolute SD. Examination stems giving two means with two SDs in different units are always CV questions wearing a disguise, and the larger CV names the more variable series.
steps.say: A small SD can still mean large relative spread. Convert both series to CV and the larger percentage wins.

rows: Compare CV, never raw SD, across units

steps.title: CV in laboratory quality control
steps.tx: Laboratories live by the **coefficient of variation in quality control**: daily control samples yield within run and between run CVs, plotted on Levey Jennings charts with warning and rejection limits at two and three standard deviations. A rising CV exposes reagent decay, pipetting drift, or instrument failure before patient results suffer. Glucose assays target CVs under about three percent in accredited laboratories.
steps.say: Labs track CV daily on control charts. A drifting CV betrays a failing assay before patients are harmed.

left.title: Healthy assay
points: Low stable CV, under 3 to 5 percent

steps.title: Quartiles divide into four
steps.tx: Ordered data quartered by **quartiles in descriptive statistics** place the first quartile (twenty fifth percentile) below which a quarter of values lie, the median as second quartile, and the third quartile at seventy five percent. Quartiles need only ordering, never normality, which is why growth monitoring, income reporting, and hospital stay summaries quote them where means would lie under skew.
steps.say: Quartiles cut ordered data into quarters. The median is simply the second quartile.

steps.tx: A box and whisker plot draws ordered data split by **quartiles in descriptive statistics**. One quarter of values sit below the first quartile, also the twenty fifth percentile, the median forms the second, and three quarters sit below the third. Whiskers run toward the outer observations, and detached points are marked as outliers. Because only rank is required, skewed hospital stays and income data can be summarised this way.
steps.say: A box and whisker plot draws ordered data split by quartiles in descriptive statistics. One quarter of values sit below the first quartile, also the twenty fifth percentile, the median forms the second, and three quarters sit below the third. Whiskers run toward the outer observations, and detached points are marked as outliers. Because only rank is required, skewed hospital stays and income data can be summarised this way.

vis.caption: A box and whisker plot labels the quartiles, the median, the whiskers, and outlying points. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.title: Interquartile range in depth
steps.tx: The **interquartile range** (third quartile minus first) captures the central half of any distribution and defines box plot fences: values beyond one point five interquartile ranges from the box edges count as outliers, beyond three as extremes. In skewed length of stay data (median four days, IQR two to seven), the IQR communicates typical variation honestly where a standard deviation inflated by one hundred day stays would mislead managers.
steps.say: Interquartile range is Q3 minus Q1, the middle half. Beyond one point five times it from the box lie outliers.

steps.title: Percentiles and centile charts
steps.tx: Generalising quartiles, **percentiles (centiles)** mark the value below which a stated percent of observations fall: the ninetieth percentile blood pressure, the third percentile weight flagging undernutrition on growth charts. The median is the fiftieth percentile. Percentile reference ranges (third to ninety seventh) define growth chart channels used daily in anganwadis and paediatric clinics across India.
steps.say: A child on the third weight percentile has ninety seven percent of peers heavier. Centiles turn one measurement into a standing.

right.title: Percentile traps
points: Not a percent score in an exam
Crossing channels matters more than one point

steps.title: Semi interquartile range
steps.tx: Half the interquartile range forms the **semi interquartile range (quartile deviation)**, an older spread measure centred on the median: quartile deviation equals (Q3 minus Q1) divided by two. It appears in legacy Indian textbooks and examinations beside probable error of older literature. Recognising it as simply half the IQR prevents the panic this antique term intends to provoke.
steps.say: Quartile deviation is just half the interquartile range. Old name, simple idea.

nodes.label: Report as quartile deviation around median

steps.title: Relative versus absolute dispersion
steps.tx: All unit free measures (coefficient of variation, quartile coefficient built from quartiles) belong to **relative measures of dispersion**, while range, IQR, and standard deviation in original units are absolute measures. Absolute measures answer how much in grams or days; relative measures answer how much compared with the average or across populations. Examination lists asking which is relative expect coefficient of variation first.
steps.say: Absolute spread carries units; relative spread is a pure percentage. Coefficient of variation heads the relative family.

steps.title: Worked examination pattern
steps.tx: The repeated **coefficient of variation examination pattern** gives two groups with means and standard deviations and asks which is more variable or more consistent: compute both CVs, award variability to the higher and consistency to the lower. A second pattern asks the measure comparing spread across different units (answer CV) or the middle fifty percent spread (answer IQR). Both dissolve once definitions are reflexes.
steps.say: Two means, two SDs, different units: compute CVs. Higher CV varies more; lower CV is more consistent.

right.title: Stem asks more consistent
points: State both CV values as proof
